hydrocephalus/018.jpg.description:
Head CT in normal pressure hydrocephalus (left image) and head MRI (right image), in the coronal plane at the level of the posterior commissure.
In the left image, the CSF spaces over the convexity near the vertex are narrowed ("tight convexity", red circle), as are the medial cisterns (red circle) - these are typical findings of NPH. On the right image, however, the CSF spaces over the convexity near the vertex (red arrow) and the medial cisterns (green arrow) are widened, a finding consistent with brain atrophy.

whitematter/003.jpg.description:
Head CT in normal pressure hydrocephalus (left image) and head MRI (right image), in the coronal plane at the level of the posterior commissure.
In the left image, the CSF spaces over the convexity near the vertex are narrowed ("tight convexity", red circle), as are the medial cisterns (red circle) - these are typical findings of NPH. On the right image, however, the CSF spaces over the convexity near the vertex (red arrow) and the medial cisterns (green arrow) are widened, a finding consistent with brain atrophy.

cerebellum/001.jpg.credit: A patient with typical clinical features of mitochondrial encephalopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) but without an obvious genetic cause: a case report
cerebellum/001.jpg.description: (a) A computed tomography brain scan showing bilateral basal ganglia calcification; the cerebellum shows prominent folia indicating mild cerebellar atrophy. (b) Axial T2 brain magnetic resonance image scan showing left temporo-parieto occipital ischemic lesion. (c) Axial T2 brain magnetic resonance image scan showing the extension of the parietal temporal region to the occipital lobe, and also showing a right occipital lesion. (d) Magnetic resonance spectroscopy showing inversion of J-coupling phenomenon at 1.3 ppm, indicating lactate peak. Abu-Amero et al. Journal of Medical Case Reports 2009

ftd/001.png.description: The neuropathology of case III:12. (A) C7 cervical cord showing symmetrical Wallerian degeneration of lateral corticospinal tracts and anterior corticospinal tract. Note atrophy of anterior nerve roots in comparison to dorsal nerve roots. TDP-43 immunopositive skein-like (B) and punctate (C) cytoplasmic inclusions within anterior horn cells of the spinal cord. (D) Normal TDP-43 positive nuclear staining of the anterior horn cell. (E) Anterior horn cell showing Bunina bodies. (F) Spongiosis in layers 2 and 3 of parasagittal motor cortex.
